about: The phrase “Cálicem salutáris” comes from Psalm 115:4 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 116:13 in Hebrew): “I will take the chalice of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord.” The closing petition returns to the biblical “odor suavitátis”, a description of an offering made to the Lord (Lev 4:31).

seg.nr: The priest takes the chalice and offers it, saying:

seg.tr: Lord, we offer You the chalice of salvation, imploring Your clemency, so that it may rise before Your divine majesty with a pleasing fragrance for our salvation and that of the whole world. Amen.

fn.w005: Genitive of the neuter noun “salutáre”, dependent on “cálicem” (w004).
fn.w007: A participle referring to the unexpressed subject of “Offérimus” (w001).
fn.w016: Feminine ablative agreeing with “salúte” (w020), not a neuter plural.
fn.w020: Both “nostra” and “totíus mundi” qualify this noun.
fn.w024: Subjunctive after “ut” (w009), with the chalice as its subject.
